title: Project: Hospital Appointment and Billing Database
learningObjectives: Model patients, clinicians, appointments and invoices.
Use keys and constraints to protect appointment and billing records.
Query schedules and patient appointment history.
Define privacy, access and operational testing requirements.

understand.concept: A hospital appointment and billing database records patient identities, clinicians, appointments and charges. Each appointment is an event linked to a patient and clinician.
understand.whyItMatters: Healthcare scheduling and billing depend on accurate relationships, clear appointment states and restricted access to sensitive information.
understand.analogy: A clinic schedule links a patient visit to a clinician and a billing record, while patient identity remains in a separate register.
understand.analogyLimit: This simplified project is not a clinical record system. Real healthcare data requires strict privacy, regulatory, audit, retention and clinical-safety controls.

explain.narrative:
## Project brief
Build a compact hospital scheduling and billing database. It must store patients, clinicians, appointments and invoices, support daily schedules, show patient visit history and summarize billed amounts.

## ER design
Patients and clinicians are parent entities. Appointments reference both and record appointment time and status. Invoices reference appointments and store an amount in integer minor units for this sample.

## Data and safety rules
Use controlled appointment states, positive or non-negative amount constraints and unique keys. Avoid placing clinical notes or sensitive diagnoses in general reporting tables.

## Project assessment
Test schedule boundaries, cancelled appointments, missing invoices and multiple visits. Restrict patient information, audit changes to appointments and billing, and document that the sample is not a production clinical system.

examples.title: Create patient, clinician, appointment and invoice tables
examples.code: CREATE TABLE proj25_patients (patient_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, patient_name TEXT NOT NULL, contact_ref TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE proj25_clinicians (clinician_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, clinician_name TEXT NOT NULL, specialty TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE proj25_appointments (appointment_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, patient_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES proj25_patients(patient_id), clinician_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES proj25_clinicians(clinician_id), appointment_time TEXT NOT NULL, appointment_status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (appointment_status IN ('scheduled','completed','cancelled'))); CREATE TABLE proj25_invoices (invoice_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, appointment_id INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES proj25_appointments(appointment_id), amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (amount_cents >= 0), invoice_state TEXT NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: Creates four related entities. Each appointment references one patient and clinician; an invoice is linked to at most one appointment in this simplified model.

examples.title: Seed patients, clinicians, appointments and invoices
examples.code: INSERT INTO proj25_patients VALUES (1, 'Asha', 'contact-A'), (2, 'Bilal', 'contact-B'); INSERT INTO proj25_clinicians VALUES (10, 'Dr Rao', 'Cardiology'), (20, 'Dr Sen', 'General'); INSERT INTO proj25_appointments VALUES (101, 1, 10, '2026-11-22T09:00:00', 'completed'), (102, 2, 20, '2026-11-22T10:00:00', 'scheduled'), (103, 1, 20, '2026-11-23T11:00:00', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO proj25_invoices VALUES (501, 101, 25000, 'issued'), (502, 102, 15000, 'draft');
examples.explanation: Adds synthetic patient, clinician, appointment and invoice records. contact_ref is a placeholder and must not be treated as a real patient identifier.

examples.title: List the daily appointment schedule
examples.code: SELECT a.appointment_time, p.patient_name, c.clinician_name, a.appointment_status FROM proj25_appointments AS a JOIN proj25_patients AS p ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id JOIN proj25_clinicians AS c ON c.clinician_id = a.clinician_id WHERE a.appointment_time >= '2026-11-22' AND a.appointment_time < '2026-11-23' ORDER BY a.appointment_time;
examples.expectedOutput: 2026-11-22T09:00:00 | Asha | Dr Rao | completed; 2026-11-22T10:00:00 | Bilal | Dr Sen | scheduled
examples.explanation: Returns appointments for the stated day using a half-open timestamp range. The query excludes the cancelled appointment on the next day.

examples.title: Summarize issued invoice amounts by clinician
examples.code: SELECT c.clinician_name, SUM(i.amount_cents) AS billed_cents FROM proj25_invoices AS i JOIN proj25_appointments AS a ON a.appointment_id = i.appointment_id JOIN proj25_clinicians AS c ON c.clinician_id = a.clinician_id WHERE i.invoice_state = 'issued' GROUP BY c.clinician_id, c.clinician_name ORDER BY c.clinician_name;
examples.explanation: Groups issued invoices by clinician. The draft invoice for Dr Sen is excluded by the WHERE predicate.

examples.title: Cancel an appointment and verify the state
examples.code: UPDATE proj25_appointments SET appointment_status = 'cancelled' WHERE appointment_id = 102 AND appointment_status = 'scheduled'; SELECT appointment_id, appointment_status FROM proj25_appointments WHERE appointment_id = 102;
examples.explanation: Updates only the scheduled appointment and verifies the state. A real hospital workflow must also apply cancellation policy, audit the actor and handle billing adjustments.

practise.guidedTask: Run the schedule and billing reports. Explain why the draft invoice is excluded and why patient contact references are not exposed in the schedule output.
practise.independentTask: Extend the model with appointment rooms and clinician availability. Add tests for overlapping appointments, cancelled visits, missing invoices and access to patient contact information.
hints: Separate patient identity from appointment events.
Store billing amounts with a defined currency unit.
Use explicit columns to minimize sensitive data exposure.

questions.prompt: What does an appointment row represent?
options: A visit event linked to a patient and clinician
questions.answer: A visit event linked to a patient and clinician
questions.explanation: Appointments are events and should be modeled separately from patients and clinicians.

questions.prompt: Why use a controlled appointment_status CHECK?
options: To restrict values to approved workflow states
questions.answer: To restrict values to approved workflow states
questions.explanation: CHECK enforces the allowed state values.

questions.prompt: Why is the schedule query's date range half-open?
options: It includes the start and excludes the next day boundary
It changes the time zone automatically
questions.answer: It includes the start and excludes the next day boundary
questions.explanation: Half-open ranges avoid overlap between adjacent days.

questions.prompt: Why exclude draft invoices from billed totals?
options: They have not reached the issued state in this report definition
They belong to another patient table
questions.answer: They have not reached the issued state in this report definition
questions.explanation: The report explicitly filters to issued invoices.

questions.prompt: What is essential for real healthcare systems beyond this schema?
options: Privacy, audit, retention and regulatory controls
questions.answer: Privacy, audit, retention and regulatory controls
questions.explanation: Healthcare data requires strict operational and legal safeguards.
